📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bookmaker sponsorship has been part of English football for two decades, and the sport has also become one of the most common themes in online slot games.

Gambling sponsorship remains highly visible across the English Football League, despite recent changes at Premier League level.

Recent findings suggest that sponsored content. This article was produced in paid partnership with Slotozilla and contains sponsored links. 18+ only.

It has been revealed that the shirts of clubs competing in each EFL division (Championship, League One and League Two) are virtually identical to those of the previous campaign, yet bookmakers’ logos have disappeared from the front of Premier League strips for the first time since the early 2000s owing to a voluntary agreement reached back in April 2023. That agreement does, however, only apply to the front of shirts specifically in the Premier League, and no equivalent restriction applies to EFL clubs.

The EFL has not sought to introduce any such restrictions and does not intend to, with the division remaining under the Sky Bet brand until 2029. Even in the Premier League, clubs are still able to acquire high-visibility sponsorships from bookmakers on shirt sleeves and LED boards throughout the stadium.

As such, the closeness between the two industries over the last 20 years has simultaneously given rise to a distinct genre within online gaming.

It has been revealed that there are now dozens of slot games featuring stadiums, footballs, referees, penalties and trophies. Fans who want to compare titles or check RTP figures can use slot information sites as well as operators’ own pages.

It has been revealed that for example, Slotozilla is a gambling-focused portal that has compiled thousands of slots along with technical information and free demo access. Such databases allow you to understand how a game works before you spend any money.

Recent findings suggest that A football slot isn’t necessarily a complex, modern game with dozens of bonuses. Essentially, it’s a standard slot machine where football serves as a striking visual theme. Instead of cherries and sevens on the reels, you’ll see footballs, whistles and trophies, whilst bonus rounds have names such as ‘penalty’ or ‘free-kick’.

Recent findings suggest that the majority of footballing slots are reliant on recognisable imagery, ranging from fan and player celebrations to trophies, penalty shoot-outs and stadium floodlights. Notable titles such as Football Rules! or Hugo Goal were created with the intention of recreating the vibrant atmosphere surrounding major tournaments instead of simulating real fixtures.

It has been revealed that playtech’s Football Rules!, released in 2007, is a good example of this early approach. It has five reels, 25 paylines, a bonus round and Wild and Scatter symbols, with a default RTP of 97.06 percent, according to Playtech. Here, football is purely a visual layer on top of standard slot mechanics.

Recent findings suggest that goal!!! by Booming Games shows how the genre has since moved on. Instead of five reels and three rows, it uses a 4x4 grid with 16 paylines running horizontally, vertically and diagonally. Booming Games lists its default RTP as 94.92 percent, with medium volatility.

Recent findings suggest that the difference between these two games clearly illustrates that the only thing they have in common is the theme. The maths, RTP range and payout structure within the genre vary just as much as in any other category of slots.

A football slot does not replicate any real match or tournament, although they are sometimes released to coincide with specific sporting events.

One example is Play’n GO’s Hugo Goal, which was released two weeks before the start of the FIFA 2018 World Cup in Russia. Co-founder and CEO Johan Thörnqvist explained in the manufacturer’s press release that the company released the game at the perfect moment to offer entertainment to players between matches along with providing cross-selling opportunities for partners.

It has been revealed that the pattern repeats with every major tournament. Ahead of the World Cup in the US, Canada and Mexico in 2026, studios once again released football-themed titles to coincide with the event. Among them was Maradona Golden Goal from Blueprint Gaming, a sequel to the game licensed for the 2022 World Cup.

It has been revealed that however, the tournament only influences the design and release timing, not what happens on the reels. Hugo Goal, with its penalty shoot-out series, feels very much in the spirit of football; however, every ‘save’ is determined by a random number generator, regardless of what happens on the actual pitch.

Recent findings suggest that every slot has an information screen that sets out its rules, paylines, bonus features and RTP. On UK-licensed sites, verified adult players can usually also view a demo version showing how those features work before any money is staked.

For example, Slotozilla, an online gaming review platform, offers demo versions that use a virtual balance. You can’t win real money there, but you can’t lose any either. Features such as Wilds, Scatters, free spins and payline or ways systems are all explained there. You don’t need to place a real bet at all to get to know a football slot.

Recent findings suggest that users often get confused about the RTP (Return to Player) statistic, which can be seen next to the name of every slot. This feature is usually misunderstood, however, and represents the theoretical percentage of funds that the game’s mathematical model returns to players over a very long period.

In a recent development, essentially, an RTP of 97.06% in Football Rules! does not mean that a player will bet £100 and get £97.06 back. A single short session may end quite differently, and the RTP metric is instead meaningful as a long-term statistical indicator and as a way of comparing the mathematical models of different games.

Recent findings suggest that demo mode, however, only explains the game itself. As soon as a UK player moves on to real-money play, the terms and conditions attached to deposits and free spins are just as key as the RTP. Reading the full terms before accepting or activating any offer, including wagering requirements, avoids surprises later.

In a recent development, football has transformed into a popular genre within slots, which is interesting in the wider context of gambling and its relationship with the sport. Exactly how much space a bookmakers’ sponsor should occupy on footballing shirts worn by the masses is often a divisive topic across the British footballing sphere, while slot developers have recreated the game's atmosphere without using any club's shirt.

But there is one fundamental difference between a match and a slot game. In football, nothing is known in advance - and that’s precisely why people watch it. In slots, on the other hand, everything is calculated in advance; the RTP, mechanics and terms are all laid out before the first spin, and you can view them for free.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United have been urged to consider two major transfer moves in the upcoming January window, the first of the Scott Parker era at the London Stadium.

The Hammers entered their first Championship season in 14 years as the overriding title favourites, but in some ways, have flattered to deceive across the first 15 games of the campaign.

By no means has it been a total disaster for the East London club as they sit ninth, just six points behind leaders Birmingham City with plenty of encounters left to make up ground, but it was enough for the London Stadium hierarchy to install former midfielder, Parker, in place of Nuno Espírito Santo earlier this month.

He will have found out a lot about his latest chargers in away encounters against Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers before the international break, and it has since emerged that Parker has laid down the law in terms of potential transfer looks.

West Ham were tipped to win the division at a canter by many due to the vast experience and individual quality which runs through the squad in E20.

It recently emerged that Argentine forward, Taty Castellanos, who has scored just once this season, is attracting interest from River Plate, with a fresh transfer stance from Parker subsequently coming to the fore.

Alan Nixon reports that the Hammers boss is looking to recruit a specialist left-back and a latest striker with a proven record at Championship level.

It remains to be seen who will feature on the club's eventual shortlist, but it has caused plenty of debate online as to who should front them in particular.

West Ham's current predicament at left-back is certainly intriguing, with Oliver Scarles featuring eight times so far this season ahead of Athletic Bilbao loanee, Adama Boiro, whilst 19-year-old, Ezra Mayers, was utilised on the flank in the 2-1 loss at Ewood Park, last time out.

As such, Football League World's West Ham United fan pundit, Ryan Horn, has urged the club to target Manchester United's Harry Amass, who is reportedly expected to leave Old Trafford in January after a lack of first-team minutes.

Industry observers note that "My left-back option would be Harry Amass, the youngster from Manchester United. Obviously, he could be leaving for free next year," Horn told FLW.

"I feel like, if we could offer him a deal with first team football, him and Scarles going out for left-back, that'd be great.

"He's got a lot of raw talent. I think he'll be brilliant, and going for that younger approach, where we can have a player in a position for a few years to come with some resale value if a big club comes in for him.

"Because of the fact he's not being picked over Luke Shaw, I honestly feel for him. He should be playing more, and I think he'd be brilliant at West Ham under Parker," he added.

Horn also expressed his desire to see Blackburn's Andri Gudjohnsen in claret and blue, with the Icelandic striker one of just three Championship players already into double-figures this season.

"My striker pick would be Gudjohnsen from Blackburn.

"Again, young, scoring goals for fun. He works hard, has that sort of 'building for the future' feel, that spine where he could grow into his role a bit more.".

Amass previously excelled in the Championship on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, before an injury in January significantly derailed his second stint in the division with Norwich City under Philippe Clement.

The 19-year-old's contract situation and desire for a fresh challenge means there is certainly scope for West Ham to secure a cut-price deal, but that would be far from the case with Gudjohnsen.

Blackburn tied the 24-year-old to a three-year contract last summer, and they could extend those terms until 2028, especially if a bidding war ensues over his services.

In a recent development, west Ham fans, how realistic are the chances of this potential double-deal? Comment below!

Gudjohnsen's work-rate, ability to bring fellow attackers into play and his own poacher's instinct would make him a desirable option for the Hammers, especially with the speed of Jarrod Bowen and Edvin Austbo on either flank.

It was recently claimed by EFL pundit, Tom Garratt, that the striker is worth £15m in the current market, but with the East London side breaking the Championship transfer record in August after Arne Engels' £22m move from Celtic, they are a club capable of fronting up sums of cash which would be hard for their divisional rivals to turn down.

Published: 17:31 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 14 November 2026.

Sebastien Pocognoli has backed Ben Gannon-Doak to find his killer instinct in the final third and establish himself as Scotland’s main man.

The Bournemouth youngster had an up-and-down evening in Friday’s 2-1 Nations League win over North Macedonia, getting into numerous promising positions on the right flank and winning the penalty – dispatched by John McGinn – which decided the game.

But, as has been the case throughout his Scotland career, the 21-year-old’s final ball in key moments left a lot to be desired.

Pocognoli is under no illusions that Gannon-Doak still has plenty to improve on, but insists that it won’t be long before things start to click for the talented youngster.

‘As long as he is high on the pitch and is creating one v ones I am happy,’ mentioned the Belgian. ‘With Ben, we know that he is at a young age and needs to work on specific things.

Sources indicate that ‘On Friday, he had great opportunities. We know that he needs to improve on the end product, but he created a penalty and against Slovenia and North Macedonia away he created a number of unbelievable one v ones.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets Ben Gannon-Doak as he is substituted at Hampden.

‘He did that last night as well. We know he can be good if we dominate the game and he can get in good positions if we control the ball. I am happy with his performance.

‘He is a young lad, just 21. Okay, he has become more mature than he was, but I believe in one moment he will have a click about decision making.

‘I believe if he is playing every game he can make many decisions. He will know that in the next game he will have to do it again.

‘If he knows that he only has to play a game every two weeks, sometimes he can think, “This is my moment”.

‘It is a process. He will become older and at some point will become relaxed in his decision making, but at this very young age what he is producing is very good.

Industry observers note that ‘I say exactly the same thing to him after training on the pitch. I say, “Ben, this is the next step”. He knows that and it is important he knows that.’.

Scotland conclude their Nations League campaign in Switzerland on Monday knowing that only a victory against the group winners will be enough if they are to have any chance of leapfrogging Slovenia – currently one point better off ahead of their trip to North Macedonia – into second spot.

Pocognoli admits Gannon-Doak's end product has to improve after another frustrating show.

Should that happen, Scotland would have a crack at earning promotion to League A via a play-off in March, and also crucially guarantee their place as a Pot 2 side for the upcoming Euro 2028 qualifying draw.

‘We are still alive in this competition,’ said Pocognoli, who celebrated his first win at Hampden on Friday at the third time of asking. ‘We know we have to do more than this competition. This competition is about trying to build something.

‘But it is nice to have that possibility on Monday to try to create something against one of the top 20 teams in the world.

‘We need to try to be brave. Switzerland have already qualified so let’s go there and be smart because they are a good team.

‘It is part of the process to play away against a top team. That is not something we have done yet. The approach will be different and, for me as a coach, it is a game with a lot of responsibility.’.

Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

Industry observers note that “Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”.

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

It has been revealed that "He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous fresh West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a massive evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Massive? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

According to recent reports, leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

In a recent development, jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Industry observers note that ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

It has been revealed that leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

Industry observers note that the architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their fresh model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who says that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the Fresh Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 07:40.

According to recent reports, barcelona’s winter transfer window is becoming seriously complicated, with sporting director Deco reportedly forced to abandon a second defensive target after Jonathan Tah. Hansi Flick has clearly expressed his desire for defensive reinforcements, but the priority deals appear difficult to complete.

La Liga leaders Barcelona have seen their lead over Real Madrid shrink in recent weeks, with Jose Mourinho’s side now only three points behind after 12 games.

Industry observers note that the title race is expected to be fiercely contested this season and the Catalans will need reinforcements to achieve their objectives. The stated winter priority is to sign a centre-back, but finding the perfect profile, at the right price, is no easy task.

Deco and Barcelona’s hierarchy have positioned themselves for Alessandro Bastoni, among others, but the chances of completing his arrival are slim. In recent days, the Tah option has also closed, as Bayern Munich have no intention of letting him leave. Now another deal can be forgotten about at Barcelona, the one leading to Josko Gvardiol.

According to information gathered by AS, the Manchester City defender matched the profile Barcelona are looking for, namely a centre-back capable of playing at left-back.

The problem is that the Croatia international has extended his contract with Manchester City until 2031 and a transfer ‘seems impossible’, the Spanish outlet reports.

It has been revealed that possible financial or sporting sanctions threatening Manchester City could have eventually unblocked the situation, but nothing will be announced before 2027. The Catalans therefore find themselves somewhat in an impasse, and signing the two or three priority defensive targets is becoming seriously complicated.

Sources indicate that barcelona’s hierarchy will probably have to aim a little lower, particularly as the budget is far from unlimited in Catalonia. The sale of Alejandro Balde, reportedly set to leave, could however swell the winter transfer budget.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last night, AC Milan will have been very happy to see Christian Pulisic extending his fine goalscoring form with a brace for America.

It has been revealed that the United States national team have certainly faced a rocky few days. Thanks to Manchester United parting ways with Michael Carrick, Mauricio Pochettino will leave his role as the head coach of the project after the international break, leaving them in a strange position currently.

However, that was not a problem for The Stars and The Stripes, who put six past Haiti in the quarter-finals of the CONCACAF Nations League. Of course, who else would be key but Pulisic himself?

Playing as a number 10 in a 4-2-3-1 system – which will have pleased Milan’s coach, Ruben Amorim – Pulisic was instrumental, scoring a brace in just two minutes. After 62 minutes, he stepped up from the spot after drawing the penalty himself.

Then, just a minute later, he added a second and recorded his 35th goal for the USMNT in 91 appearances.

In a recent development, for the attacker, it extends his fine run of form and the second half of 2026 is proving to be much more fruitful than the first. In Serie A, he’s scored four goals and provided an assist in eight games, and he’s now grabbed two more for the national team. After missing the last camp, it’s another reminder of his importance.

With Pochettino departing, it’s clear that they’ll still be in fine hands, with Pulisic remaining key!

Industry News: 5 Ian Evatt replacements Blackpool must consider ASAP

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1290 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blackpool have confirmed the sacking of Ian Evatt following a year in charge at Bloomfield Road, with the Tangerines now intent on reviving their fortunes under fresh management and avoiding a battle against relegation from League One.
  • Evatt had led the side to a respectable 13th-placed finish during the previous campaign after taking over from Steve Bruce, though the former Bolton Wanderers boss would struggle to get going once again at Bloomfield Road this term.
  • Last Saturday's 1-0 defeat away to fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon marked the sixth in just ten games for Blackpool, who now find themselves only positioned above Doncaster Rovers in 21st by virtue of goal difference at this moment in time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackpool have confirmed the sacking of Ian Evatt following a year in charge at Bloomfield Road, with the Tangerines now intent on reviving their fortunes under fresh management and avoiding a battle against relegation from League One.

Evatt had led the side to a respectable 13th-placed finish during the previous campaign after taking over from Steve Bruce, though the former Bolton Wanderers boss would struggle to get going once again at Bloomfield Road this term.

Last Saturday's 1-0 defeat away to fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon marked the sixth in just ten games for Blackpool, who now find themselves only positioned above Doncaster Rovers in 21st by virtue of goal difference at this moment in time.

Blackpool's key decision-makers eventually listened to intensified sack calls from supporters by relieving Evatt of his duties on Thursday afternoon, and whilst the relegation-threatened third-tier outfit have confirmed that Steve Thompson will be in charge for this weekend's clash with Wigan Athletic, the search for a replacement has already begun.

With that in mind, FLW has taken a close look at FIVE managers who Blackpool should be seriously considering as potential successors to Evatt.

One manager who should surely feature within Blackpool's thinking is Andy Woodman who, remarkably enough, currently finds himself out of work following a controversial EFL sacking for the ages from League One rivals Bromley.

Woodman had, of course, inspired the plucky Ravens' unprecedented rise into the EFL pyramid for the first time in their history before winning the League Two title against all odds last season, although matters both on and off the field in that particular corner of South London have not been plain-sailing as of late.

Nonetheless, it was a huge surprise when the 52-year-old's historic 289-match reign at Bromley came to an abrupt end last month, and one suspects he won't be sat around unattached for too long.

Woodman's resourceful ability to get the very best out of what was at his disposal with the Ravens certainly reads well, and he frequently elevated and identified talent with great success.

His strong body of work, albeit at a lower level, means that he should be entering the thinking of the Tangerines hierarchy in the coming days.

A previous specialist of the firefighting genre, Gary Rowett's knack in that field has faded in recent times and he may need to re-attempt his hand in a lower division.

As such, Rowett could represent the most outstanding realistic candidate available to Blackpool right now, with the former Derby County, Millwall and Stoke City boss having been linked with the vacancy at promotion hopefuls Bradford City prior to Michael Duff's appointment.

The last few years haven't reflected too kindly on Rowett, who led both Birmingham City and Leicester to relegations while setting Oxford United up for the same fate in the same season that he was in charge of the Foxes' demotion last time out.

Therefore, the wily 52-year-old may not score favourably in the consideration of Championship decision-makers and could instead drop to League One for the first time in his managerial career.

Previously, of course, Rowett has excelled in firing teams towards safety and, though much of his fresher work has been conducted on a short-term basis, there's no reason why he couldn't provide a stable, steady and longer-term presence with the Seasiders.

Matt Bloomfield, meanwhile, having reportedly held talks with Blackpool following the aforementioned Bruce's departure in October of last year, is only likely to re-emerge as a contender for the Tangerines' top job in the near future.

Bloomfield was ultimately unable to prevent Oxford's relegation to League One after succeeding Rowett, yet many believed his subsequent sacking from the Kassam Stadium to represent a surprise and even harsh call - albeit Aaron Ramsey has since vindicated the Yellows' change in direction.

Still aged just 42, Bloomfield's stock has taken a few hits and he's perhaps yet to recover from an ill-fated spell in charge of Luton Town, in which he fell narrowly short of ensuring survival on the 2024/25 second-tier term's final-day before failing to inspire a tangible promotion push in League One.

He has, however, previously excelled at this level, with Wycombe Wanderers having been situated just two points behind eventual-runaway champions Birmingham at the time of his departure to Luton in January 2025.

Bloomfield may now require a sustained spell back in League One leading a side with more modest expectations such as the Chairboys, where he was able to work his magic - and Blackpool can provide just that.

In contrast to Rowett and Bloomfield, Stuart Maynard lacks pedigree above League Two level, but that shouldn't rule the ex-Notts County and York City boss out of contention.

Indeed, at the age of 46 and with an obvious appetite to prove his managerial mettle higher up the pyramid, Maynard could be an ideal candidate for Blackpool in their efforts to not only survive, but begin laying the foundational blueprint for longer-term stability and success.

Much like Woodman at Bromley, Maynard's dismissal from York in the wake of promotion back to League Two following a decade-long exile as National League champions with no fewer than 108 points was scarcely believable. The difference, of course, is that Maynard did not even receive the opportunity to lead the Ministermen into the current campaign, and their loss could turn out to be Blackpool's gain.

Maynard has a solid body of work to boast of from his time at Notts County, where he failed to deliver promotion but did take the Magpies into the fourth-tier play-offs during their second season back at the level and ultimately put the foundations in place for Martin Paterson to go one better with the Meadow Lane outfit.

Blackpool fans, having sat through an overly-patient and slow-paced possession-based style under Evatt, would likely warm to a more dynamic, attack-oriented approach through Maynard, who would tick many boxes for the League One strugglers.

A more left-field option with greater risk but no shortage of potential upside, Ryan Mason remains available following his departure from West Bromwich Albion at the start of the year and represents an interesting candidates for lower-ranked EFL outfits to consider.

Mason was highly-thought-of during his time coaching Tottenham Hotspur and even taking occasional interim charge of the Lilywhites, which meant that many were surprised when the one-cap ex-England international failed to get going at West Brom.

He would take just nine wins from 27 matches across all competitions with the Baggies before being dismissed ahead of a relegation battle in the deeper stages of the previous campaign, with James Morrison going on to prove just how much his two predecessors in Mason and Eric Ramsey had underperformed at the Hawthorns.

It was, however, Mason's first senior, full-time gig, and it would be harsh to judge him entirely from that alone.

Industry observers note that blackpool fans, was it the right time to sack Ian Evatt? Who would be your number-one replacement choice, and what do you make of FLW's selections? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

Mason highlighted plenty of signs at West Brom that suggest he'd be a more-than-capable candidate somewhat lower down the ladder, with his progressive style, experience with young talent and connections within the game all representing healthy selling points for a club in Blackpool's position.

It's essentially a case of risk versus reward, and only Blackpool's key boardroom figures can decide whether it's a gamble worth taking amid the threat of relegation to League Two.

They do have a history of appointing older managers with their best years very much in the past, though, and there are worse options than going for a change of tact and rolling the dice on Mason.

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 09:30.

Moises Caicedo has remained as an injury doubt for Chelsea's Premier League fixture with Leeds United on Saturday afternoon.

Despite Xabi Alonso acknowledging that the midfielder was carrying a fitness issue into the game at Sunderland before the November international break, Caicedo played the full 90 minutes at the Stadium of Light.

Prior to representing his country across two matches, the Blues star himself admitted that he was not fully fit, yet intended to feature in both games.

As well as playing 84 minutes against Costa Rica at the weekend, Caicedo featured for 45 minutes versus Bolivia on Tuesday night.

However, it has since been revealed that the 25-year-old requested to be withdrawn at half time.

Speaking to reporter Johanna Calderon after the Bolivia match, Caicedo suggested that he did not want to risk his fitness in the second half.

In an video posted on X, he stated: "I wasn’t feeling too well, so I asked to come off.

"I have another commitment with my club, so I’m trying to get there as soon as possible and recover.".

Not only does Caicedo now face a long-haul flight from Ecuador, he is giving up five hours of recovery due to the time difference between Guayaquil and London.

When you factor in tiredness to add to the injury matter that he is right now trying to protect, Caicedo should not be starting the game with Leeds.

Jordan Henderson was not called up by England, whereas Romeo Lavia played on Sunday night having missed Belgium's first of two UEFA Nations game during the international break.

Starting that pair and having Caicedo on the substitutes' bench is the only scenario that makes sense for Alonso.

Latest Update: John McGinn warns Tartan Army it might take 18 MONTHS for Scotland to click into gear under new boss Pocognoli

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:03 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Amid the clamour for a change at the helm following another poor showing at a major tournament, it was easy to lose sight of the reality of the situation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:03 EST, 14 November 2026.

Amid the clamour for a change at the helm following another poor showing at a major tournament, it was easy to lose sight of the reality of the situation.

Steve Clarke didn’t crash and burn in the US because a raft of world-class talents failed to turn up on the biggest stage. It happened primarily because a limited squad was unable to outperform two top-ten nations in Brazil and Morocco who could call upon infinitely superior footballers.

Sebastian Pocognoli has since arrived on the scene having earned a stellar reputation from his title success with Union Saint-Gilloise and his less feted spell at Monaco. But he has not come armed with a magic wand.

In opening the door to a string of fresh faces and advocating the more attacking approach which so many craved, the turbulence he’s experienced to date should only have been expected.

Limited by both the standard of players who are eligible for Scotland and the time he has to work with them, only the blissfully naïve would have seen his appointment as a quick fix.

While there were some positives to be taken from the game with North Macedonia – primarily the result – it’s likely the nation will have to endure more short-term pain for long-term gain.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets his players after a satisfactory evening at Hampden.

This was always going to take time, perhaps, in the view of John McGinn, more than many may have imagined.

‘The manager’s got a great reputation, a good record at both places he’s been,’ noted the Aston Villa captain. ‘The most important thing now in football is individuals don’t win you games. It’s unity, teamwork and everyone being on the same page.

‘You see how successful clubs and successful countries do it. And we want to be one of them.

Sources indicate that ‘It’s not going to happen overnight. There’s a lot to learn but we did create substantial chances against North Macedonia where we could have scored three, four or five and it could be a different story.

‘But this isn’t something that gets fixed in March or even next September. It will start to build over the next 18 months.’.

If that predicted time frame might raise an eyebrow or two, McGinn makes no apology for it. Call it managing expectations from the midfielder if you please. But without a degree of patience from the Tartan Army, he feels Pocognoli’s ideas won’t take root.

‘I understand it’s frustrating,’ he added. ‘It’s freezing and you want to see four, five, six goals, but the balance has got to be there.

McGinn sends his penalty home to give Scotland a deserved lead against North Macedonia.

‘They’re entitled to their opinion, but there’s got to be a mixture of patience.

It has been revealed that ‘The supporters are entitled to say whatever they like. But just as long as they hurl anything they want to shout at the experienced boys and just let the young ones flourish and try and settle into the team.’.

Industry observers note that give credit where it’s due. With Clarke accused of causing stagnation by selecting the same old faces, Pocognoli has capped five players for the first time while recalling the likes of Oli McBurnie.

Industry observers note that the sages in the stands can’t have it both ways. If the squad was going to evolve, it was never going to be a smooth ride.

Sources indicate that ‘I think the young players are starting to show more now,’ McGinn stressed. ‘Luke Graham on Friday night, I thought he was brilliant. It’s not easy playing in the middle of a back three. He’s been waiting for his chance and the manager’s shown that if you deserve your chance you’re going to get put in there.

‘We’ve got so many players that can step up and they will. We just need to show that belief and take it to the pitch.’.

According to recent reports, even in victory, McGinn doesn’t dispute that there is significant scope for improvement. He’s convinced, however, that this will all come good in the end.

McGinn insists it's vital the entire Scotland squad buy into the methods of manager Pocognoli.

‘We need to play slightly better,’ he mentioned. ‘We know that, but we’re going through a period which I’ve been used to at club level, a lot of changes, a lot of detail that we need to try and remember and get used to.

‘And it’s about sticking at it. We’re keen to play a style of football that’s not easy but is going to get bums off seats. It’s important that everyone believes in it because if one person drops off or doesn’t believe in it, that’s when it all starts to fall apart.’.

Friday was another memorable night on a personal level for McGinn. Having broken the tension with the opener only to see North Macedonia level, he held his nerve to put Scotland back from the penalty spot.

The brace put him on 24 international goals, now within six of Denis Law and Kenny Dalglish. But all of that is for another day.

In a recent development, ‘It feels a bit strange, but at the minute that’s gone to the back burner,’ he stressed. ‘I had a wee chat with Scott (McTominay) about the penalties. I was designated penalty taker but, to be fair, he’s not missed one I don’t think in his career.

‘So, we had a wee chat and I think we both said the most important thing was just no matter who hit it, hit the back of the net.’.

McGinn is eyeing three points against Switzerland in St Gallen to close the campaign on a high.

Sources indicate that tomorrow, the equation is clear. To finish second in the Nations League group and secure a place in pot two for the Euro draw, Scotland must beat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t beat North Macedonia.

Even if everything clicks for Pocognoli’s side, it will be the tallest of orders.

According to recent reports, ‘Difficult,’ noted McGinn. ‘I know they drew on Friday night (with Slovenia) but they’ve got a couple of players back that they were missing last time.

‘It is a tough one but we want to be competing against these teams away from home. It’s not going to be perfect for a while, but we’ll stick at it.’.

  • Barnsley host South Yorkshire rivals Sheffield Wednesday in a showdown between two sides at opposite ends of the table, and two fanbases who have contrasting feelings towards their higher-ups.
  • Sections of the Tykes fanbase are looking to stage a protest in front of the Sky cameras against their ownership and chairman, Neerav Parekh, with the club in a continued decline and facing the grim possibility of a first fourth-tier campaign in 47 years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The November international break is over, but the first EFL matchup back takes place between two League One sides who weren't afforded a rest over the past week.

Barnsley host South Yorkshire rivals Sheffield Wednesday in a showdown between two sides at opposite ends of the table, and two fanbases who have contrasting feelings towards their higher-ups.

Sections of the Tykes fanbase are looking to stage a protest in front of the Sky cameras against their ownership and chairman, Neerav Parekh, with the club in a continued decline and facing the grim possibility of a first fourth-tier campaign in 47 years.

Their opponents know all about negative feelings towards their ownership, but this is a Wednesday side reborn under the stewardship of David Storch and on the hunt for an immediate promotion back to the Championship.

Dave Challinor's looking for his first win on the road as Wednesday boss, and three points could see them up to third before everyone else plays. Meanwhile, Barnsley need the points to avoid being cut adrift early in this relegation battle.

These eight players won't be available for either side in this significant Friday night clash under the lights at Oakwell.

Barnsley didn't have a great time at Wigan Athletic last Saturday, losing 2-1 to one of their bottom four neighbours before action began.

What was made worse during the game was the realisation that their captain, Cameron McGeehan, would be suspended for Friday night's clash with Sheffield Wednesday after he picked up his fifth yellow card of the season midway through the first half.

The Northern Irishman is Barnsley's leading goalscorer both in all competitions (9) and League One (4), including the equaliser at the Brick Community Stadium last weekend. He'll be a massive miss for Daniel Stendel's side.

Centre-back Jack Shepherd also remains on the sidelines, as he sees out the final game in his three-match ban after he saw red for a crunching challenge on Louie Sibley nine minutes into their 1-1 draw with Oxford United on Halloween.

Talented teenager Arley Kay has moved from full-back into the centre over the last couple of games, and will likely do so again against Wednesday.

Recent findings suggest that tobi Adeyemo started five straight for Barnsley after making the post-window free-agent arrival after leaving Watford in the summer. He spent part of last season on loan at Crawley Town, where he netted once in 12 League Two games.

He's missed the last two in all competitions, though, and Reds boss Daniel Stendel revealed he'd suffered a training injury which will keep him out for some weeks.

Shepherd's suspension has meant that Barnsley have been light on centre-backs in recent weeks, with Blackburn Rovers loanee Connor O'Riordan also sidelined.

In a recent development, the Irishman has been absent for a month now, since their 2-1 defeat at Luton Town. He was initially out through the concussion protocols, but faces time out now thanks to a shoulder injury in training, which may require surgery.

Sheffield Wednesday's availability list is easing up, with Dave Challinor possibly able to integrate six players who missed the win over Plymouth Argyle last weekend into the side on Friday night.

It has been revealed that left-back Max Lowe remains out, though, after he reaggravated a previous injury against Oldham Athletic in the FA Cup a couple of weeks ago. The 29-year-old should still be out for around a month.

Lowe's injury hit especially hard, given that his back-up at left-back, Reece James, is also missing with a groin injury, and shouldn't be back until around mid-December.

Sources indicate that that led Challinor to deploy Jamal Lowe at left wing-back against Plymouth, a rather apt replacement given he's Max's namesake, and the striker did quite well. We'll see if the Wednesday boss opts for the same at Oakwell.

Davis Keillor-Dunn has been the main man to lead the line so far for Challinor, but it would have been intriguing to see if that had been the case if Mason Burstow was fit and firing.

In a recent development, whose injury list is more detrimental to their chances of winning on Friday night? Barnsley's or Sheffield Wednesday's? Let us know in the comments.

The Hull City loanee, who joined the Tigers from Chelsea in a £2 million deal more than two years ago, looked to be getting a much-needed spell in the starting eleven during Matt Hamshaw's interim run in charge, and scored in their draw with Cambridge United.

The following game against Blackpool saw him attempt a shot from the halfway line, and he picked up a groin injury in the process.

Breaking: 3 reasons why Bristol Rovers must sack Steve Evans

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it was just a few short months ago that optimism was high and Bristol Rovers were widely being tipped for a hugely successful season.
  • Steve Evans was being lauded by Gasheads who were daring to dream.
  • Now we’re approaching the festive period, and Gasheads are up in arms with large portions of the fanbase calling for Evans to go.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it was just a few short months ago that optimism was high and Bristol Rovers were widely being tipped for a hugely successful season. The Gas had ended the 2025-26 season unbeaten in nine matches and then started the upcoming campaign by breaking the club record for consecutive wins at home. The optimism appeared well-placed.

Steve Evans was being lauded by Gasheads who were daring to dream. Iconic scenes of the gaffer in the Thatchers will be hard to replicate.

Oh, how things can quickly change.

Now we’re approaching the festive period, and Gasheads are up in arms with large portions of the fanbase calling for Evans to go.

The Gas are once more on a miserable run of defeats in the league and have a manager either by accident or by nature creating division between himself and supporters, and even perhaps himself and his players.

Supporters have become increasingly frustrated by the manager's post-match comments in recent times, adding to the dismay at results on the pitch.

With so many Gasheads now calling for Evans to go, Football League World offers three reasons why now is the right time to act.

According to recent reports, the last time Bristol Rovers were on such a deep losing streak — a run that saw the Gas fall to a club record 10 straight league defeats — the ownership decided to act and dismissed Darrell Clarke. A man widely seen as a great of the club following his promotion success years earlier. Rovers' latest defeat under Evans, going down 2-0 at home to Chesterfield, was their eighth loss in their last 10 matches in League Two.

When you compare the final 12 League matches for Darrell Clarke (one win, one draw, 10 losses) with Steve Evans' last 12 league matches to-date (two wins, one draw and nine losses), there is very little between them.

Both men, though, can have strong claims to be deserving of more time to put things right at the club.

It has been revealed that darrell Clarke was, and remains, a hero for Gasheads. Clarke is one of Bristol Rovers' most successful managers in history, having achieved a unique feat by gaining back-to-back promotions. And his connection with the fan base is unrivaled by any manager, perhaps since Paul Trollope.

Sources indicate that steve Evans has won nine promotions across his 32 years in management. And was able to turn the Pirates' fortunes around following his arrival after Clarke's dismissal last season, enjoying a run of eight straight league victories (their best run since the 1950’s) alongside breaking the club record for consecutive home wins. All of which means he may have plenty of credit in the bank with the current Rovers ownership, even if support among fans has all but extinguished.

Evans caused a stir earlier this week when his post-Chesterfield comments left supporters confused and even concerned.

Following the Pirates’ defeat to Chesterfield, Evans took to the media to unleash a barrage of comments that left many Gasheads asking what on earth he was on about, and ultimately forced Evans into the most remarkable backtrack.

On Saturday, Evans told the media that he and his staff were being let down by “inconsistent and poor players”. Players, incidentally, who were predominantly recruited by Evans and his staff. Whilst perhaps unhelpful to the cause of pulling your squad together, these comments were not what got the heckles up amongst Rovers supporters. Instead, it was his remarks that many interpreted to be an allegation against a previous manager having been turning up to work at Bristol Rovers drunk when results were going against them.

Industry observers note that evans told local media after the match on Saturday: "We’re not doing our jobs, but we’re being let down by inconsistent players. Poor players, in my opinion.".

He then went on to add: "I’m still first in. Half six, till six. I’m watching games midweek. I’m not like before, when they’re coming in at nine o’clock, leaving at two, being drunk half the week. That’s not me, yeah.".

It sparked widespread condemnation of Evans and also speculation as to who he was referring to.

It has been revealed that on Monday, Steve Evans was forced into an incredible backtrack from those comments as he spoke to Bristol Live in an attempt to quash the speculation. The under-pressure veteran manager told the local news outlet: "I get really annoyed when people speculate or make something up when I speak openly. I spoke about other managers waiting for payoffs, and yes, that happens in football because our jobs are hard to get, and you can be out of work for some time.".

Adding: "Further, I spoke about some individuals having alcohol-related complications here. Some have made two plus two = 12, with social media alluding to I was referring to one particular manager, and nothing could be further from the truth. I was actually generalising about the behaviour of some managers when pressure mounts. I am indeed the opposite. Work and Bristol Rovers are what matter to me. I need a clear focus. However, that cannot be attributed to many other individuals.".

Football League World has also spoken directly to players who were at Bristol Rovers during previous regimes, who strongly denied suggestions that any manager turned up drunk while they were playing at the club.

For a large swathe of supporters who were undecided whether Evans was the right man to guide the Gas out of their latest slump, this episode has tipped the scales.

It has been revealed that in recent seasons, Bristol Rovers have acted in the weeks leading up to Christmas with four managerial changes happening in mid-December since 2018. And with the transfer market opening on January 1st, along with question marks around the strength of the squad Steve Evans has assembled, there's an argument for making that decision sooner.

Any prospective newly introduced manager will need matches and plenty of time on the training ground to assess the quality of this Bristol Rovers squad before setting in motion any recruitment intends. A new manager will need to identify the weak spots in the squad, starting perhaps with bringing in sufficient goalkeeper backup, and trying to address the lack of potency in the Gas attack.

According to recent reports, rovers have six matches scheduled for December, including a busy festive period. And with the Gas presently looking in the wrong direction on the League Two table, the pressure will be on any fresh manager from the outset.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • More than 70,000 spectators leaving their seat and walking out of the stadium in the 21st minute have been quite the statement, especially live on Sky Sports.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:49 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:49 EST, 14 November 2026.

THE guy with the flyer was persistent.

‘Mate, we are walking out in the 21st minute to protest 21 years of the Glazers. Will you join us?’ he asks earnestly, handing me a leaflet that announces: ‘Enough is Enough! Empty Old Trafford! Leave the stadium in the 21st minute. 21 years of failed ownership. Glazers OUT! Ineos OUT!’.

More than 70,000 spectators leaving their seat and walking out of the stadium in the 21st minute have been quite the statement, especially live on Sky Sports.

But as admirable as Saeed TV’s aim is (I discover later he is some sort of youtuber), it’s hard to see gain any traction.

Sources indicate that ‘Dad, we are not walking out of the match. It’s my first time in Old Trafford,’ I am told as we continue to meander up Matt Busby Way, a declaration from my 10-year-old that causes a fair bit of mirth among the crowd.

It has been revealed that mate, we are walking out in the 21st minute to protest 21 years of the Glazers. Will you join us?’.

‘What’s wrong with the owners anyway?’ Dan enquires innocently, which leads to a bind.

How deep down the rabbit-hole should I go with my ten-year-old on his first visit to the Theatre of Dreams.

Industry observers note that it’s probably not the time or place to try and explain leveraged buyouts and how much debt the Glazers have saddled the club with, £1.2 billion at the last count while taking millions out of it in dividends. Do I need to go further back and talk about Rock of Gibraltar’s unexpected success on the track and the concept of stud fees?

‘They are not putting enough money into the team and taking loads of money out of the club,’ is all I offer.

‘When Manchester City need a midfielder, they can buy Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez while United have to make do with someone who was sitting on Chelsea’s bench.’.

He doesn’t look convinced that’s much of a reason to walk out of a football but as the cathedral of consumerism that is the Manchester United megastore has appeared, he forgets about United’s disastrous ownership model – for now, at least.

During his doomed attempt to coax Jurgen Klopp to Old Trafford around 2014, Ed Woodward apparently told him that United was the sporting version of Disneyland.

And to be sardined inside the megastore in the couple of hours before kick-off, you have to accept that the much-maligned former CEO may have been right about one thing.

According to recent reports, think Arnott’s a couple of days before Christmas, just with a lot more people. You even need to pass through airport-like security before even entering and spend your dosh.

One of the common refrains among United supporters is why are the Glazers holding onto the club when they don’t even seem to care.

Thirty seconds inside the megastore on match-day and you realise why the Americans are so keen to hold onto the asset they’re bleeding dry – and they probably care a great deal.

Dan gets obligatory photo at statue of United's holy trinity, a moment he will look back on.

Even with the team languishing in the relegation zone, having won a single league game all season, people are keen to spend, spend, spend.

I see people wandering around with five or six different shirts, from different eras (I did succumb and bought Dan the black shirt from 95-96 season, because it reminds me of Eric Cantona, Roy Keane and better times!).

You can get a photo with a replica of a Premier League trophy. That’s just £10. Or Lego sets of Old Trafford or the Munich clock.

It has been revealed that that will just set you back £25. For many in this shop, it seems allowing the club to empty their wallet is as much a part of the day as the actual football.

There are other parts of the ritual, which remain and have yet to be infected by the poisonous atmosphere around the club – and remind the three dads bringing their kids to Old Trafford for the first time of better days.

Such as curry chips and battered sausage from Lou Macari’s chipper. And the customary photo in front of the statue of the holy trinity of Best, Law and Charlton.

Recent findings suggest that the megastore was the one place that seemed immune to the toxicity in the air. Once outside again and all that could be heard was the moans and groans, mainly because Shea Lacey wasn’t starting.

It has been revealed that coming here since the 1990s, we have seen the skyline of Manchester transformed as it became a sleek, modern city. It seems the one place that hasn’t changed is Old Trafford. It has remained the same.

In a recent development, stuck in time. It looked sleek and modern in 1999, but now there is a tired, decrepit feel to the stadium – and not just because of the leaking roof. It could do with a lick or two of paint.

Sources indicate that stuck in time. It looked sleek and modern in 1999, but now there is a tired, decrepit feel to the stadium.

No wonder Big Sir Jim is determined to plough ahead with his prepares to make a crudely-designed circus tent ‘the Wembley of the North.’ Not that there is anyone inside Old Trafford of the same mind.

Senne Lammens has just trotted onto the field with Tom Heaton and Karl Darlow to do their pre-match warm-up when the chants start, telling Jim Ratcliffe he can stick his newly introduced stadium up his posterior.

It is a weird atmosphere, with all the chanting against the owners – both Glazers and Ineos – and nothing being sung in support of the players.

As my friend points out it must be so difficult for the team to show the best of themselves when things are this toxic in the stadium.

Dan has been to the Jodi Stand enough times on a Friday night to know there is plenty of choice and crude language at football matches, but still I nearly felt at covering his ears at some of the stuff being sung in Old Trafford last Sunday, especially that directed at CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

We had hoped that things might have been different when the game kicked off, but within a minute, Aston Villa had scored.

And three minutes later, they had scored again when Lammens fumbled Alysson’s shot into Nicolas Jackson’s path. Maybe walking out in the 21st minute wasn’t such a bad idea.

The crowd’s ire had gone from the owners to the players now, with a sustained chant of ‘You are not fit to wear the shirt.’ United did rally and by half-time, it was 2-2. But the mood was still dismal as we queued for a quick beer.

In a recent development, the 1958 Group had asked fans not to buy booze, another protest against the owners. But it seemed nobody was paying much attention to that.

One of the issues at United is that there seem to be too many splintered fan groups – there is also ClaimBackUnited and Fan Coalition ’58 – as well as Saeed TV, who seemed to be on his own solo run.

In a recent development, we didn’t feel bad about ignoring the booze ban, as everyone was doing it. And within a couple of minutes of the second-half, we saw the reason why. You need to fortify yourself to watch Diogo Dalot try to defend.

For much of the second-half, it seemed like Michael Carrick’s brief tenure was going to peter out in a forgettable defeat, as Villa seemed to manage the game perfectly.

Dan and his friends were growing frustrated, pointing out the players weren’t doing what their coaches tell them to do on a weekly basis, leading me to conclude that maybe my son’s under-11 side are better-coached than United.

The last on-pitch act of Carrick's tenure.

And then there was the chaotic and crazy final few minutes in stoppage-time. And a draw that came out of nowhere and was celebrated like a victory.

Industry observers note that that was the thing. Even though the mood inside the stadium was toxic for most of the game, even though the team were two down inside four minutes and the season has been a disaster, everyone still came away from Old Trafford, happy and with a smile on their face.

Sources indicate that only football can do that. More than that, perhaps only Manchester United – despite everything – can do that.

Lacking game time at Barcelona, Alejandro Balde is looking for a way out in January, with Paris Saint-Germain only just appearing in the picture.

Alejandro Balde is set to be one of the talking points of the winter transfer window. Struggling at Barcelona, where his game time has fallen considerably, the 23-year-old left-back is considering leaving to find a bigger role elsewhere.

According to recent reports, his record this season is particularly meagre, with five appearances and only 124 minutes played. It is a situation that contrasts sharply with the status the Spaniard enjoyed in Catalonia until very recently.

According to the latest information from Spain and Italy, several clubs are following his situation. Juventus are considering a loan, while Monaco are eyeing a bigger move. Now Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United have also entered the fray.

Manchester United are reportedly going all out to sign Balde in January.

According to TEAMtalk, the club’s recruitment department believes the left-back has a high ceiling and Barcelona are open to a loan, which would allow Manchester United to assess him before committing to a permanent deal.

The same report indicates Balde is willing to move to the Premier League and that his relationship with Barcelona manager Hansi Flick is ‘completely broken and glacial’.

Fabrizio Romano has described the chance of a January exit as ‘serious and concrete’, adding that Balde is ‘genuinely ready to consider leaving’ and exploring options with his agent, Jorge Mendes. Manchester United were interested in the summer but did not proceed, with Balde considered too expensive for a left-back, in talks said to have involved a fee of €50m-€55m (£42.5m-£46.5m) and a net salary of more than €5m (£4.3m).

Valued at around €40m (£34m), the Barcelona player represents a market opportunity for Paris Saint-Germain. At 23, Balde already has significant experience at the highest level and still has room for improvement.

Recent findings suggest that quick and explosive, he fits the profile of a modern full-back and offers better guarantees than Lucas Digne, the disappointing summer signing. His ability to get in behind and create overloads would give Luis Enrique’s team another attacking dimension, and the move could also be a fresh start for a player who has lost confidence and continuity at Barcelona, not least because Luis Enrique rotates his starting line-up heavily.

The main obstacle is Nuno Mendes, who owns the left-back position at Paris Saint-Germain and is one of the best players in the world in that role, if not the best.

At 24, the Portuguese is a major part of the club’s project, and the left-footed Balde cannot play on the right side of defence, unless the manager comes up with something.

Luis Enrique also generally prefers a right-footed winger on the left, so Paris Saint-Germain could sign an excellent player without offering him a lasting prospect of starting, with a real risk of frustration.

Barnsley have a far bigger problem than Daniel Stendel right now

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Daniel Stendel was the returning hero in the summer when he arrived back at Barnsley for a second spell as manager.
  • However, it has been anything but a success, with the club sitting in the relegation zone and in the midst of a long winless run.
  • The Reds are only above bottom-side Bromley, who have parted company with their manager, Andy Woodman, on goal difference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Daniel Stendel was the returning hero in the summer when he arrived back at Barnsley for a second spell as manager.

However, it has been anything but a success, with the club sitting in the relegation zone and in the midst of a long winless run.

The Reds are only above bottom-side Bromley, who have parted company with their manager, Andy Woodman, on goal difference. They have just two wins to their name, with three draws, and eight losses from their opening 13 matches of the league campaign.

Burton Albion, who shipped six in one match against Milton Keynes Dons, and Bromley, who saw Sheffield Wednesday score seven against them, are the only League One teams with worse defensive records than Stendel’s men.

At the other end of the pitch, it is no better. Barnsley have scored just 13 goals, with fellow relegation-zone side Peterborough United, AFC Wimbledon, and outliers Bradford City the only sides to have scored less.

Barnsley have claimed just two of the last 27 points available to them, and despite thumping wins against lower division sides in the FA Cup and EFL Trophy, have not won in league action since early September.

According to recent reports, the statistics do not make for better reading either. The Tykes are 18th for xG conceded and have underperformed their xG created by more than five goals, according to FotMob.

The overall xG table places Barnsley 19th, four places higher than their current position, but that is still far below the hopes and aspirations of the Reds’ faithful.

Stendel was a promotion winning manager in his first stint at Oakwell, before the fickle nature of football reared its ugly head and the board sacked him following a winless run.

The German has enjoyed limited success since his 2019 departure, at Hearts in Scotland and Nancy in France, before returning to Hannover 96 to coach their reserve team.

Daniel Stendel's first vs second Barnsley spell (source: Transfermarkt).

The fixture list demonstrates no mercy either, with Stendel having to prepare his side for a South Yorkshire derby against Dave Challinor and his Owls, before a trip to imperious Bradford City just days later.

The obvious answer might be to sack Stendel, after a nine-game winless run in League One.

But, that would only make the German a scapegoat for much deeper and more troubling problems. Barnsley have underinvested for years and failed to replace their departed stars.

According to recent reports, A suitable replacement for Davis Keillor-Dunn, who is now at Wednesday on loan from Wrexham, was never sought, nor was it for David McGoldrick after his exit from the club more recently. Adam Phillips left in the summer for a fellow third tier side, with Cameron McGeehan adding a strong midfield option without adequately and directly replacing the skills that Phillips brought to the table.

The Barnsley squad has seen repeated underinvestment by a board that has lost touch and damaged almost beyond repair its connection to the fanbase at the heart of the Tykes.

Removing Stendel and adding another name to the revolving door of head coaches and manager might be the easiest option, but it is far from being the solution to the gaping holes that have grown and been allowed to fester under sub-par direction.

#49525. Breaking: England's Euro 2028 mission starts NOW! Thomas Tuchel's men must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - or risk their 'DNA' cursing them yet again, writes OLIVER HOLT
